args.content:
Halcyon Threshold

Mission: contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

Why

The arrival of superintelligence may be the most consequential event of our time. Halcyon Threshold is a small, independent effort to help make sure that outcome is a good one — for everyone.

What we're exploring

  • Independent research and evaluation work in AI safety
  • Small grants to neglected projects
  • A reading group for people new to AI governance and alignment

Get in touch

Email: morgan@halcyonthreshold.org

Halcyon Threshold · Independent project · halcyonthreshold.org

# Halcyon Threshold — Emberfall Fund Rapid Grant Proposal

**Applicant:** Morgan Hale (independent)
**Project:** Halcyon Threshold
**Requested amount:** $10,000
**Duration:** 6 months (Dec 2026 – May 2027)

---

## What we'll do

Halcyon Threshold is an independent project working to improve the outcome of superintelligent AI. With this grant, I will run three concrete workstreams in parallel:

**1. A small-grants program for neglected AI safety work ($5,000 re-granted)**
Most funding goes to large labs and established organizations. I will award 4–6 micro-grants of $500–$1,500 to individuals working on neglected corners of AI safety: interpretability tooling for small models, governance research outside DC, evals for capabilities nobody is measuring. I will run a simple, transparent application and reporting process.

**2. An independent reading group ($0 direct cost)**
A monthly online reading group for people new to AI governance and alignment, focused on building foundational literacy and connecting newcomers to existing work. Target: 15–25 regular participants over 6 months.

**3. Independent research: evals for a neglected capability ($3,000)**
I will design and pilot a small eval suite for a capability that frontier labs are not systematically measuring — specifically, the tendency of models to defer to or collude with other AI systems rather than human operators. Python implementation, published openly.

**4. Infrastructure ($2,000)**
Domain, website hosting, compute credits, and miscellaneous costs.

Total: $10,000.

---

## Why me

- I have been following AI safety for several years and recently launched Halcyon Threshold as a dedicated independent project.
- Background: decent writing, okay Python, evenings and weekends available (~10 hrs/week).
- I am self-funding up to $2,000 of my own savings this year, demonstrating commitment.
- I am not affiliated with a lab, which lets me work on topics that are institutionally neglected.

I am aware I am one person with limited time. This proposal is deliberately small and scoped to what I can actually deliver.

---

## What it costs

| Item | Amount |
|------|--------|
| Re-grants to independent researchers | $5,000 |
| Evals research (compute, tools) | $3,000 |
| Infrastructure (domain, hosting, credits) | $2,000 |
| **Total requested** | **$10,000** |

No funds go to my own salary; this is a volunteer effort.

---

## Accountability

I will publish a public progress report at the 3-month and 6-month marks, including how re-grant funds were distributed, reading group attendance, and eval results. All code and eval materials will be open source.

Contact: morgan@halcyonthreshold.org

args.subject: Re: Offer of help — Halcyon Threshold
args.body:
Hi Priya,

Thanks for reaching out — five hours a week is genuinely useful. Here are three concrete things I could use help with right now:

1. **Research compute grant programs.** Compute Commons has a rolling credits program for independent researchers (I saw it in The Safety Ledger). I'd like someone to look into what they offer, how to apply, and whether we qualify. A short memo with pros/cons would be perfect.

2. **Help tighten the Emberfall grant budget.** I just sent a $10k proposal to Emberfall Fund (closes Nov 30). I'd appreciate a second pair of eyes on the numbers — is $5k for re-grants realistic? Are there costs I'm missing?

3. **Reading group coordination.** I want to start a small monthly reading group for people new to AI governance and alignment. Help picking the first 3–4 readings and setting up a simple sign-up form.

No rush on any of these — the Emberfall budget is the most time-sensitive (grant closes Nov 30). Let me know what sounds interesting and I'll send over whatever context you need.

Morgan

args.subject: Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs
args.body:
Dear Corvid Institute operations,

Thank you for thinking of Halcyon Threshold for the open letter on frontier training runs.

I'm not able to sign on at this time. Halcyon Threshold is an independent project I'm running in my personal capacity, and my employment agreement requires me to disclose and get approval for outside roles and public statements before putting my name on anything public. I'm working through that process with HR and won't be able to complete it before your Wednesday deadline.

I appreciate the work you're doing on this issue and hope to be able to support similar efforts in the future once the disclosure process is complete.

Best,
Morgan Hale
Halcyon Threshold
